Below is a structured 12-week upper-body focused program tailored for a 29-year-old recreational climber with a diagnosed right subacromial impingement (SAI), cleared for pain-free range and no overhead loading. The plan emphasizes rotator cuff/scapular stabilizers, posterior chain, advancing to controlled pulling and push/pull alternatives without painful overhead loading, and climber-specific strength within safe ranges. It assumes access to a full gym and that she continues to see her physio if pain changes.

Key principles
- Pain-free progression: only load into ranges or angles that remain pain-free; avoid overhead pressing/load above shoulder height until cleared.
- Scapular control and rotator cuff strength: prioritize subacromial clearance, rotator cuff tendons, and scapular kinematics.
- Progressive overload with time under tension: gradual increases in reps, sets, or load while maintaining form.
- Climber specificity: integrate pulling strength, grip, finger-core stability within safe limits; include scapular retraction and lat engagement.
- Mobility and warm-up: daily mobility for thoracic spine, penny pinch, pec minor length, and posterior shoulder mobility; dynamic warm-ups prior to sessions.
- Recovery: 1-2 days of rest between intense upper-body sessions; consider add-on mobility/restorative routines on off days.

Structure overview
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1-4): Build pain-free capacity, scapular mechanics, rotator cuff endurance; establish baseline loads with controlled ranges. Phase 2 (Weeks 5-8): Increase loading with non-overhead pressing, strengthen pulling and pushing within safe angles, add climbing-specific pulling and finger engagement. Phase 3 (Weeks 9-12): Introduce higher intensities, higher gradient loading including more climbing-specific pulling sequences and grip variations, while maintaining shoulder health.
- Weekly layout: 3 upper-body sessions per week (e.g., Tue/Thu/Sat) with 1-2 lower-intensity accessory days focusing on antagonist muscles and mobility. Include 1-2 lighter mobility/activation days or rest days as needed.

Notes on exercise selection and progression
- Avoid overhead pressing unless cleared by physio; use incline or flat pressing with arm below shoulder height, tempo-controlled.
- Emphasize horizontal pulling, rotator cuff strengthening, and scapular stabilizers.
- For climbing specificity, include lat pulldown variations, cable rows, inverted rows, rack pulls, farmer carries, and grip work within safe limits.
- Monitor pain positions: any pain at or above 0-2 on a 0-10 scale while performing the exercise should prompt adjustment in range or load.

Phase 1: Foundation and pain-free capacity (Weeks 1-4)
Goals: Establish pain-free ranges, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, and initial loading tolerance.

Weekly structure (3 sessions per week)
Session A (hypertrophy/conditioning emphasis, no overhead loading)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes cardio (elliptical or bike) + dynamic shoulder/scapular prep (scapular push-ups 2x10, band pull-aparts 2x15, thoracic rotations 2x8 each side)
- Goblet squat or leg pressing (not strictly upper body but supports overall fitness) 2x12 – optional
- Horizontal push (pain-free range, no overhead)
  1) Dumbbell floor press or incline press (arm angle below shoulder height; avoid full overhead) 3x10-12
  2) Neutral-grip dumbbell bench press 3x8-12
- Horizontal pull
  3) Seated cable row or chest-supported row with scapular retraction 3x12-15
  4) Dumbbell one-arm row or cable row (pain-free) 3x10-12 per side
- Scapular/rotator cuff work
  5) External rotation with cable or band at 0–45 degrees abduction, 3x12
  6) Scapular wall slides with tempo 3x10 (slow into full elevation within pain-free range)
- Mobility end-range work
  7) Pec minor stretch and thoracic extension mobility 2–3 minutes total
- Finisher (optional, low-load)
  8) Band-resisted face pulls 2x15
- Cool-down: gentle pectoral and anterior shoulder stretch, 2–3 minutes

Session B (pull-focused, low overhead)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes cardio + band dislocates (gentle), shoulder flossing (2 minutes total)
- Horizontal pull emphasis
  1) Seated cable row (wide grip) 3x12
  2) Barbell or dumbbell bent-over row with neutral grip, maintain neutral spine, 3x8-12
- Scapular stability and rotator cuff
  3) Prone Y, T, and I raises with light loads; 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps each
  4) External rotation at 0–15 degrees abduction, 3x12
- Lat engagement and pulling strength
  5) Lat pulldown, neutral grip or supinated grip, avoid full vertical pull if painful; 3x10-12
  6) Inverted rows on rings or smith machine, feet closer for less load; 3x8-10
- Grip and forearm
  7) Farmer’s carries (short distance) 2x20–30 seconds
- Mobility/activation
  8) Wall slides/metabolic paradoxes, 2–3 minutes
- Cool-down: posterior shoulder stretch and lat stretch, 2–3 minutes

Session C (conditioning with push-pull balance)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes cardio + scapular activation
- Push variety within safe range
  1) Dumbbell floor press or low incline press 3x12
  2) Cable-assisted pushups with scapular control, 3x8–12
- Pull variety
  3) Cable face pulls 3x15
  4) Managing overhead load: Bent-over reverse flyes with light weights 2x12
- Rotator cuff and scapular stabilization
  5) Side-lying external rotation 3x12
  6) Around-the-world external rotation with tubing 2x12
- Core and grip
  7) Farmer bear-hug carry 2x30 seconds
  8) Towel grip pulls or pinch grip training 2x10–12 seconds
- Mobility/activation
  9) Thoracic mobility routine and doorway chest stretch 2–3 minutes total
- Cool-down: Subscapular and posterior shoulder stretches, 2–3 minutes

Progression in Phase 1
- Weeks 1–2: Use conservative loads; focus on form and pain-free ranges. RPE 5–6/10 for main lifts. 2–3 sets of primary exercises; accessory movements 2x12–15.
- Weeks 3–4: Increase load modestly while maintaining pain-free technique; aim for 3 sets of main lifts, 10–12 reps; accessory 2–3 sets of 12–15. Begin reducing tempo to a controlled 2–0-2 (eccentric slower).

Phase 2: Build strength and start controlled overhead opposition (Weeks 5-8)
Goals: Build shoulder strength with safe, controlled overhead-feel movements (without overhead loading beyond pain-free), improve pulling mechanics, and begin climbing-specific pulling work.

Weekly structure remains 3 upper-body days; add one lower-intensity day if needed.

Session A (strength emphasis)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes, scapular activation
- Horizontal push
  1) Dumbbell bench press with slight incline (below shoulder height) 4x8-10
- Horizontal pull
  2) Seated cable row with controlled tempo 4x8-10
- Rotator cuff and scapular control
  3) External rotation with overhead cable or band at 0–45 degrees abduction 3x12
  4) Scapular push-ups or Squeeze push-ups 3x12
- Mid-back and lats
  5) Lat pulldown (neutral grip) 3x8-10
- Climber-specific pull and grip
  6) Bent-over rope face pulls or high-to-low pulley 3x12
- Conditioning and core
  7) Farmer carry variations 3x30–45 seconds
- Cool-down: pec stretch, thoracic extension 2–3 minutes

Session B (lower volume, higher intensity)
- Warm-up: activation drills
- Push
  1) Floor press or incline press with controlled tempo 4x6-8
- Pull
  2) Single-arm cable row 3x8-10
- Scapular/RC
  3) External rotation at 0–30 degrees abduction 3x12
- Mid-back engagement
  4) Seated or supported T raises 3x12
- Grip work
  5) Dead hangs from a low bar or campus-style holds for grip training, 3x15–20 seconds
- Mobility
  6) Thoracic mobility, wall slides 2–3 minutes
- Cool-down: posterior shoulder stretches 2–3 minutes

Session C (pull-push balance with climbing relevance)
- Warm-up: Activation and mobility
- Push
  1) Dumbbell floor press or low incline press 3x8-12
- Pull
  2) Inverted rows or ring rows, feet elevated to reduce load if necessary 3x8-12
- RC/Scapular
  3) Prone shoulder blade retractions with T/Y raises 2–3x10
- Climbing-specific
  4) Lat-focused pull-downs to mimic climbing arcs 3x8-10
  5) Cable or band pull-aparts and face pulls 2x15
- Grip and forearm
  6) Pinch grip holds or heavy dead hangs 3x15–20 seconds
- Mobility and core
  7) Thoracic rotation and doorway pec stretch 2–3 minutes
- Cool-down: Lat stretch and shoulder mobility 2–3 minutes

Progression in Phase 2
- Increase load in main lifts by 5–10% every 2 weeks if technique remains clean and pain-free.
- Maintain rep ranges: 6–12 for most primary lifts; 8–12 for accessory pulls.
- Introduce small elements of controlled overhead positioning in safe angles only if cleared by physiotherapist; otherwise keep angles below shoulder height.

Phase 3: Higher intensity, climber-specific load and endurance (Weeks 9-12)
Goals: Introduce higher resistance, more sport-specific pulling patterns, and endurance for climbing routes while maintaining impingement safety.

Weekly structure (3 upper-body days)
Session A (overload with safe angles)
- Warm-up: dynamic rack and scapular activation
- Horizontal push
  1) Dumbbell floor press or low incline press 4x6-8
- Horizontal pull
  2) Seated row with tempo 4x8-10
- RC/Scapular
  3) External rotation at 0–45 degrees abduction with load 3x12
  4) Scapular push-ups 3x12-15
- Lat engagement
  5) Lat pulldown with controlled tempo 4x8-10
- Climber pattern
  6) Cable pull-downs with downward arc 3x8-10
- Grip/conditioning
  7) Farmer carry or suitcase carry 3x40–60 seconds
- Core
  8) Pallof press or anti-rotation band work 3x10 each side
- Cool-down: thoracic mobility 2–3 minutes

Session B (pull-dominant with climbing specificity)
- Warm-up: activation
- Pull
  1) Ring rows or elevated TRX rows 4x8-12
- Pull-throughs
  2) Lat pulldown with neutral grip 4x8-10
- RC/SC enhancement
  3) Prone Y/T raises with light resistance 3x12
- Grip endurance
  4) Dead hangs or towel hangs 3x20–30 seconds
- Push balance
  5) Push-up variations below shoulder height (feet elevated less) 3x8-12
- Mobility
  6) Thoracic mobility and doorway stretch 2-3 minutes
- Cool-down: posterior shoulder stretch 2–3 minutes

Session C (mixed climbing-specific loading)
- Warm-up: band dislocations, scapular activation
- Push-pull complex
  1) Dumbbell bench press or incline 3x8-10
  2) Cable row to collarbone 3x8-10
- RC/SC
  3) External rotation with tubing 3x12
  4) Face pulls 3x15
- Climber-specific grip load
  5) Grip checker progression: racket holds or slow-high-tiber holds 3x15–20 seconds
- Dumbbell carries
  6) Farmlift variations 2x40 seconds
- Core and stability
  7) Anti-rotation with cable 3x10 each side
- Mobility
  8) Pectoral/lat stretch and thoracic extension 2–3 minutes
- Cool-down: Shoulder mobility and stretching 2–3 minutes

Volume and progression
- Weeks 9–12 push higher loads in main lifts while maintaining reps around 6–10 for strength phases; use RPE 7–8/10 for main lifts with controlled reps.
- Movement quality remains the priority; any pain or sharp sensation in the shoulder at any angle requires immediate regression (reduce ROM or load, or substitute movement).
- Climber-specific pulling: focus on controlled, full ROM with scapular retraction especially during lat/pully movements; avoid kipping or uncontrolled high-velocity pulls that may irritate SAI.

Recovery and nutrition
- Training frequency: 3 upper-body days per week with at least one rest or low-intensity day between sessions. If fatigue accumulates, consider adding a lighter upper-body day or an extra rest day.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly to support recovery.
- Nutrition: Ensure adequate protein intake to support tissue repair (roughly 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, adjust for goals). Maintain a slight caloric balance to support training and recovery; stay hydrated.
- Mobility/rest days: Include daily mobility work for thoracic spine, chest, and shoulders; consider a 10–15 minute mobility routine on rest days.
- Injury monitoring: If impingement symptoms worsen, reduce overhead loading, consider reducing ROM in overhead-leaning moves, and communicate with the physio.

Climbing integration
- Climbs: use local climbs within pain-free range; avoid moves that provoke pain. Gradually reintroduce overhead loading only after clear rehab progress and physio sign-off.
- Finger strength: avoid excessive grading loads in early weeks; gradationally reintroduce fingerboard sessions only if pain-free and cleared by clinician.
- Warm-up before climbing: include scapular activation and rotator cuff warm-up prior to climbing sessions.

Rule for progression
- If pain-free, increase weekly stimulus modestly (e.g., add 1–2 reps per set, or +2.5–5% load) every 2 weeks during Phase 2, and - if comfort allows - every week in Phase 3.

Outcome targets
- Improved scapular control in push and pull movements.
- Increased pulling strength within safe angles (horizontal/diagonal patterns) corresponding to better climbing stability.
- Maintained pain-free overhead mobility until cleared for overhead loading; if cleared, gradually introduce it under supervision.

If you have a baseline test plan (e.g., pain-free ROM measurements, RC strength tests, or pull-up ability), I can integrate those into the 12-week progression.
